_comment: One-line summary per source directory (paths relative to src_overrides/bedrock/, nested since ADR 0003). Required by scripts/check_memory.py: a new directory fails CI until it is described here. Consumed by scripts/gen_memory.py to build MAP.md.

bookmarks.summary: Bookmark store: folders and tags together, search over title, URL and tags. Item 35. Mirrors Chromium's components/bookmarks placement.

devtools.summary: Added DevTools privacy panels. Rule zero: never break an upstream Chromium panel. Item 36.

downloads.summary: Download manager: honest pause/resume derived from Accept-Ranges, attacker-chosen names and MIME types treated as untrusted. Item 33.

extensions.summary: Chromium-compatible extension API plus generated capability disclosure; an update can never grow an extension's powers. Item 23.

extensions/catalog.summary: Curated privacy-extension catalog (JSON data + validator) and the recommendation engine whose job is to say no. PrivacyTools.io brief.

fuzz.summary: libFuzzer harnesses for every untrusted-input entry point, each also built as a deterministic CI smoke run via -DBEDROCK_FUZZ_SMOKE. Item 43.

history.summary: History store whose hard requirement is deletion: removing an entry removes the derived ranking data too. Item 35.

omnibox.summary: Omnibox input classification only — Chromium's own providers still rank bookmarks, history and tabs. Item 7.

passwords.summary: Local password store, platform keystore encryption, no sync and no server. Item 34.

perf.summary: Performance budgets measured on every commit; unmeasurable budgets are marked pending instead of claimed. Item 46.

privacy/core.summary: The Privacy Engine core: feature registry, the PrivacyPolicy resolver (single source of truth for ten layers), per-site Protection Controller, security-level presets, zero-telemetry policy. Items 8, 11, 25, 39, 45.

privacy/fingerprinting.summary: Anti-fingerprinting policy and deterministic value derivation: normalize first, never random per call, 21 documented surfaces. Items 9-10.

privacy/network.summary: Network privacy: DNS settings (named resolvers, fail-closed strict mode), HTTPS upgrading and per-host certificate exceptions, WebRTC IP exposure modes. Items 16-18.

privacy/security.summary: Security baseline audit: forbidden Chromium-weakening switches are rejected in tests, so privacy work cannot ship a less safe browser. Item 24.

privacy/stats.summary: The one privacy event log feeding DevTools panels, Privacy Center and the per-site shield, so the numbers cannot disagree. Items 36-38.

privacy/storage.summary: Cookie and storage isolation: one StorageKey decides where every backend reads and writes, cache, DNS and HSTS included. Item 15.

privacy/tracker_blocker.summary: Content blocking: ABP/uBO-syntax filter engine (independently implemented, rarest-token index), the behavioral Privacy-Badger-style heuristic, and the single BlockingPipeline::Evaluate() every request goes through. Items 12-14.

profiles.summary: Profiles, which share nothing by default, and New Identity — the controlled session reset that also states what it does not erase. Items 21-22.

search.summary: Search engine selection per context (default / private / Tor), pure logic feeding TemplateURLService. Item 6.

session.summary: Browsing modes: Normal, Private and the optional Tor transport with circuit isolation. Tor lives here rather than in its own tree because it is a transport, not a subsystem. Items 19-20.

settings.summary: Settings surfaces: the Privacy Center dashboard and the privacy configuration (posture) view. Item 37, brief item 19.

settings/knowledge.summary: Privacy Knowledge Center: native offline articles (layer A) kept separate from externally licensed material (layer B) for licensing reasons.

themes.summary: Theme engine: 5 modes, 14 live properties, contrast validation, and no 'restart required' apply kind. Items 27-29.

ui.summary: Browser UI surfaces: tab model with two layouts, optional sidebar, per-site privacy panel. Items 30-31, 38.

updater.summary: Provider-agnostic update system: signature-verified, works without any project-run infrastructure. Item 40.

workspaces.summary: Workspaces: named sets of tabs and visual settings inside one profile — an organisational boundary, never a privacy boundary. Item 32.
